# PEN-4023 — report the timeout bound that fired, not the one in config

Issue: [PEN-4023](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/PEN/issues/PEN-4023)
(split from [PEN-4016](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/PEN/issues/PEN-4016) §7(a))

## Files

- `src/server/execute.ts`
- `src/server/execute.test.ts`

## What changed

Every agent Job in production carries `spec.activeDeadlineSeconds: 7200`
(verified live across two companies and three agents). This adapter did not put
it there — `buildJobManifest` omits the field entirely when `config.timeoutSec`
is 0, which it is on every agent, and the adapter logs `(deadline: none)` on
the same run the Job object carries the two-hour deadline. Kubernetes enforces
the object, not the belief.

`waitForJobCompletion` already observed the `Failed` / `reason:
DeadlineExceeded` condition that marks such a kill, and then discarded the
condition, returning only a boolean. The caller formatted the error as
`` `Timed out after ${timeoutSec}s` `` — interpolating this adapter's own
configured value — so a run Kubernetes killed at 7200 s reported **`Timed out
after 0s`**, and the bound that actually fired was recorded nowhere. Eleven runs
across two agents were lost to this, eight of them clustered in a 105-second
window at 7248–7305 s; the signature was obvious and unreadable, because nobody
can grep for a number that is never written down.

Changes:

- `waitForJobCompletion` now returns an optional `timeoutBound: { source,
  seconds }` alongside `timedOut`. On the `DeadlineExceeded` branch it reads
  `spec.activeDeadlineSeconds` off the same Job object that carries the
  condition — the condition's own message is a fixed string with no number in
  it, so `spec` is the only place the value exists. The non-deadline `Failed`
  branch and the `Complete` branch are unchanged.
- `timedOut` has three causes with three unrelated bounds, and only one of them
  is `timeoutSec`; `source` names which. A new optional sixth parameter lets the
  bounded post-watch-error re-check label its 60-second budget
  `adapter_state_recheck` rather than have it read as a configured run timeout.
- New exported `describeFiredTimeoutBound` renders the message. An observed
  bound always beats the configured one; when the two disagree the message says
  both (`Timed out after 7200s (Job activeDeadlineSeconds; adapter
  timeoutSec=0)`), because the disagreement is the finding; and an unknown
  bound is reported as unknown rather than falling back to a configured `0`,
  which would reconstruct the very string this removes.
- The timeout return now carries `resultJson: { observedTimeoutSec,
  observedTimeoutSource, configuredTimeoutSec }`. The server reconciles these
  in `buildHeartbeatRunStopMetadata` so the stored record can no longer assert
  `timeoutFired: true` beside `timeoutConfigured: false`.
- `waitForJobCompletion` is now exported for tests. Driving the
  `DeadlineExceeded` branch through `execute()` needs a full running-pod and
  log-tail fixture that would pin a dozen unrelated behaviours alongside it.

No timeout value is changed, added, or removed by this change, and no kill
behaviour moves — PEN-4023 is explicitly scoped to the bookkeeping half.
Whether the two-hour kill should exist at all is PEN-4016 §7(b), an owner
decision, and who writes the `7200` is still unattributed (PEN-4016 §4). This
fix reads the bound at runtime, so it needs neither answer.
